newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Rouble lower with T-bills, on bank client sales.
newsitem.headline: Rouble lower with T-bills, on bank client sales.

text.p: The rouble edged down on bank client selling and dealers said a downward trend on the Treasury bill market implied investors were seeking fewer funds for Wednesday's government securities auction.
On May 28 the Russian Finance Ministry will auction 6.50 trillion roubles of 308-day GKO discount Treasury bills and 4.00 trillion roubles of 728-day OFZ bonds.
roubles/dollar May 27 midday May 27 early May 26 close
NOTE - Monday was U.S. Memorial Day. Russian banks use U.S. banks for settlement.

"T-bills have gone down further today and less funds were put aside for this market. Besides, rouble demand turned out to be low as tomorrow's auctions do not seem very attractive for investors," Menatep Bank dealer Mikhail Zaretsky said.
He added the dollar was also supported by bank clients' orders to sell roubles.
A Rossiisky Kredit Bank dealer said the rouble felt more pressure from players closing long positions opened on Monday in anticipation of rouble demand ahead of the auctions.
